en: The body is the finest of trees; five are its branches.
Into the restless mind Time has entered. ||||
Make it firm, and take the measure of the Great Bliss:
Lui says, ask the guru and know. || refrain ||
All the samādhis [?]: what are they done for?
Through pleasure and pain one surely dies. || refrain ||
Cast off the bond of desire [?] and the hope in the craft [?] of the senses [?];
take the side of the Void [?] close to you. || refrain ||
Lui says: I have seen it in meditation [?];
dhamaṇa and camaṇa, the two, I sat on as my seat [?]. || refrain ||
rom: lui bhaṇa:i guru pucchia jāṇa || dhru ||
eṛieu chāndaka bāndha karaṇaka pāṭera āsa
sunupākha bhiti lāhu re pāsa || dhru ||
dhamaṇa camaṇa beṇi pāṇḍi ba:iṇa || dhru ||
notes: The language of the Charyapada (an early stage of Bengali, close to the Apabhraṃśa of the time) is old and the songs speak in a deliberately veiled 'twilight language' (sandhyābhāṣā) of Buddhist tantric practice: many words have more than one accepted reading, and editors and translators differ on several lines of this song. The translation follows the plainest sense of the words; the [?] marks show where it is least sure.

Romanization: ISO 15919 applied to the Bengali letters of Shastri's edition, as on the site's other Bengali songs: the inherent vowel written (ḍāla, kāla), ব as b, ড় as ṛ, ঁ as m̐; the colon marks a vowel letter standing after a (pa:iṭho, bhaṇa:i, karia:i, ba:iṇa), so that a + i is not read as the diphthong ai. The double dandas are given as ||; the editor's bracketed letters (স[মা]হিঅ) are kept.
|| refrain ||: ধ্রু (dhru, for dhruvapada) is the edition's mark of the refrain; the doubled double danda after line 2 (॥॥) is printed as in the source.
line 1: kāā is the body (kāya); tarubara, 'the best of trees'; 'pañca bi ḍāla', 'five (are) the branches': commonly read as the five senses or the five aggregates (skandhas) of Buddhist teaching.
line 2: cīe, 'in the mind' (citta); kāla is time and also death; pa:iṭho, 'has entered'.
line 3: diṭa, 'firm' (dṛḍha); 'what is to be made firm' is not said: usually taken as the mind. mahāsuha (mahāsukha), the Great Bliss of tantric Buddhism.
line 4: Lui (Luipa) names himself, as each Charyapada poet does.

line 5: sa[mā]hia, the edition's restoration, read as samādhi (meditative absorption) [?]; kāhi, 'why, for what'. Readers differ on whether the line asks what samādhi is for or says that all of it is useless.
line 6: nicita, 'surely' (niścita); mariāi, '(one) dies'. Often read as saying that one who clings to pleasure and pain, even through such practices, still dies.

line 7: the line is among the least certain [?]: chāndaka bāndha, 'the binding of chanda' (desire, will; also deceit or a scheme); karaṇaka pāṭera āsa, 'the hope of the karaṇa's pāṭa' (karaṇa: the senses, or ritual practices; pāṭa: craft, order, a seat). eṛieu, 'give up, cast off'.

line 8: sunu, 'the Void' (śūnya); pākha, 'side, wing' (pakṣa); bhiti is read as 'clinging, drawing near' or as 'wall'; 'lāhu re pāsa', 'take (it) to your side'. The sense of the whole line is disputed [?].
line 9: āmhe, 'we, I'; sāṇe is read as 'in meditation' (dhyāna) [?]; diṭhā, 'seen'.

line 10: dhamaṇa and camaṇa are left untranslated: they are usually explained as two channels or two breaths of the yogic body, sometimes as two contrary forces, which the yogi masters; pāṇḍi read as 'seat' [?], ba:iṇa as 'sat, seated' [?]; beṇi, 'both, the two'.
